problem.title: Literature status of open Erdős problems: a first set of thirty-four
problem.done_when: Every problem has a status agreed by two different vendors, each naming the strongest published result by title, authors, year and identifier, with a quote from it.

problem/*.brief: Problem {n} of this set is number {p.number} in the Erdős problems database kept by Thomas Bloom, filed under {p.tags}, where it reads: {p.statement} The task is a literature check of this one problem: find the strongest published result toward it, in a journal paper, a preprint with an arXiv number, or a proof the database records among its proof expositions, and return the problem's status as the literature stands. Proved means the statement as posed is proved, or the question answered yes; disproved means a counterexample or a proof of the negation is published, or the question answered no; solved means it is settled another way, such as a quantity the problem asks for being determined; open means no published work settles it, whatever partial results exist. Evidence: the result's title, authors, year and venue; its arXiv number as two whole numbers, the four digits before the dot and the digits after it read as a number (so 02384 is given as 2384), both zero when it has none; one sentence saying what the result establishes; and a quote of at most 40 words from the result that states it. With no published result at all, the title is none and the year 0. Identifiers, never links.
